source.prompt: Instrumental background music for a classic 1990s-style Japanese fantasy role-playing game. The writing and orchestration evoke the golden age of 16-bit console RPG soundtracks (memorable singable lead melody, clear bass line, warm chords, tasteful hall reverb), but the production is high quality, warm and full, recorded with real-sounding instruments. Completely original melody. The game's world lives in an endless night lit by lanterns, lamps and great beacon fires; the score is gentle and melancholic, with warmth and a quiet, stubborn hope. A harbour town under lamplight: lanterns along the pier, sailors, a market that never sees the sun, the smell of the sea. Friendly and warm with a touch of nostalgia, a gently swinging melody that feels like home port at night; lively but not loud. Tempo 112 BPM, 4/4 time, key of G major. Instrumentation: accordion and clarinet melody, mandolin and fingerpicked guitar, harp, walking upright bass, light brushes and tambourine; acoustic instruments only, no electronic sounds, no synthesizers, no drum machines, no programmed beats, no bells or chimes. Form: 2-bar mandolin pickup; A melody on accordion; B melody on clarinet with harp, a little wistful; a short interlude on mandolin and harp; A melody again with fuller band. Duration: 115 seconds. Instrumental only: no vocals, no singing, no spoken words, no lyrics. Keep one steady tempo and key from start to finish, no fade-in and no fade-out, no long silences; the last bar leads naturally back into the first bar so the piece loops seamlessly as game background music.
